advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the reconcile-check 'no writes / safe first run' operator description with the runner's unconditional strict ticket-store delivery for all profiles.
evidence: .github/workflows/reconcile-bridge.yml:48: '          - reconcile-check   # read-only diagnostic (no lock, no writes) — safe first run'
src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:234-248: after a successful non-paused pass the runner unconditionally runs `_delivery_command` (commit-and-push --strict) for every profile

tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py:27-33: `runner_env(..., mode="reconcile-check")` then asserts `git(origin, "show", "tickets:bridge-event.txt").stdout == "event from bridge\n"` — reconcile-check DOES push ticket events
advisory.finding: The runner performs strict commit-and-push of ticket-store events for the reconcile-check profile, but the GitHub workflow's reconcile-check option is described to operators as a 'read-only diagnostic (no lock, no writes) — safe first run'. reconcile-check does not mutate Jira, but the runner still commits/pushes any inbound ticket events, so the 'no writes / safe' description understates the ticket-store side effects.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make pause-marker validation key-order-independent (compare `set(payload) == set(_PAUSE_KEYS)` / check required keys) rather than `tuple(payload) == _PAUSE_KEYS`.
evidence: src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:141: `and tuple(payload) == _PAUSE_KEYS`
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:176-182: the marker dict is built literally as {paused, reason, who, paused_at} then json.dumps'd — order match is incidental, not contractual
advisory.finding: Pause-marker recognition is coupled to the reconciler's exact JSON key ORDER: `_is_valid_pause_marker` requires `tuple(payload) == _PAUSE_KEYS`. It works only because rebar_reconciler.__main__ happens to emit keys in paused/reason/who/paused_at order. If that emission order ever changes, a genuine pause marker would be rejected and the runner would proceed to strict delivery instead of skipping it.
advisory.suggested_fix: Replace `tuple(payload) == _PAUSE_KEYS` with a set/subset comparison over the required keys so the check does not depend on JSON key insertion order.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Record a fetchable/immutable upstream source for the vendored GitLab schema (the GitLab API raw ref path) or document why the checksum-only self-check is sufficient provenance.
evidence: .github/schemas/gitlab-ci.schema.provenance.json:3-4: `"requested_github_raw_url": ...`, `"requested_github_raw_result": "HTTP 404"`

tests/unit/workflow/test_reconcile_workflow_lint.py:95-99: provenance test only asserts revision/dialect and `provenance["sha256"] == hashlib.sha256(_GITLAB_SCHEMA.read_bytes()).hexdigest()` (self-referential, not upstream-verified)
advisory.finding: The vendored GitLab CI schema's provenance cannot be independently re-derived from a public upstream: the recorded GitHub raw URL returned HTTP 404 and the verification test only checks that the sha256 matches the locally vendored file, not that the file matches an immutable upstream artifact.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Record the license/attribution of the vendored gitlab-ci schema (e.g., in the provenance file or a NOTICE).
evidence: Schema begins with `{ "$schema": ..., "$id": "https://gitlab.com/.gitlab-ci.yml", ... }` and contains no license field or header
No LICENSE reference visible for the vendored 3318-line schema file
advisory.finding: The vendored GitLab CI schema carries no license/attribution metadata inline; upstream schema licensing posture for this copied file is unverified.
scenarios: Redistributing an upstream schema whose license requires attribution

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a runner-level test that emits a single `BRIDGE_STATE: <in-flight|legacy-gated|reschedule>` on stderr with rc==0 (via the stub harness STUB_STDERR) and asserts the resulting BridgeRun `state` matches the disposition and that delivery still proceeds.
evidence: src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:158-166: `if returncode == 0: states = [line.removeprefix(_STATE_PREFIX) ... if line.startswith(_STATE_PREFIX)] ... return disposition.state, disposition.canonical_exit`

Reconciler emits these markers on rc==0: src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:60-63 (`IN_FLIGHT=('in-flight',0,3)`, `PHASE_GATE=('legacy-gated',0,4)`, `RESCHEDULE=('reschedule',0,75)`) and __main__.py:92 `print(canonical_message or f"BRIDGE_STATE: {disposition.state}", file=sys.stderr)`

Heldout test only exercises the legacy_exit fallback: tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py:22-33 parametrizes `legacy_rc` [3,4,75] via `env['STUB_RC']`, never emitting a `BRIDGE_STATE:` marker on rc==0

ABSENCE: search for `BRIDGE_STATE` under tests/scripts and `legacy-gated` under tests/scripts and tests/interfaces/facades returned no runner-level match (the only `legacy-gated` hit is tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_cli_heldout.py:448, which is at the reconciler level, not through the packaged runner result)
advisory.finding: The runner's `_classified_result` BRIDGE_STATE-marker branch (returncode==0 with a single `BRIDGE_STATE:` line mapping a benign disposition such as in-flight/legacy-gated/reschedule to the result `state` before proceeding to delivery) is never exercised end-to-end. The heldout legacy-benign test drives STUB_RC=3/4/75, which hits the separate legacy_exit fallback branch (lines 167-169), not the STATE-marker branch (lines 158-166). A regression that mishandled the rc==0 STATE marker (e.g. defaulting state to 'converged', or misclassifying it as operational_failure) would pass all current tests.
advisory.suggested_fix: In test_run_reconcile_bridge_heldout.py add a parametrized test setting env['STUB_STDERR']='BRIDGE_STATE: legacy-gated\n' with STUB_RC=0 and asserting completed.returncode==0 plus the emitted state; ideally also assert via rebar.bridge_run() that result['state']=='legacy-gated'.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a runner test where the reconcile subprocess cannot start (e.g. remove/clear the rebar stub or point PATH away from it) and assert returncode==1, no delivery/push occurs, and the 'could not start rebar' diagnostic is preserved.
evidence: src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:217-219: `except OSError as exc: stderr += f"Reconcile failed: could not start rebar: {exc}\n"; return _result(profile, "operational_failure", 1, ...)`
ABSENCE: search for `could not start rebar` across the repo returns only the source line (src/rebar/_bridge_runner.py:218); no test asserts this diagnostic
tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py:88-101 always plants a valid executable `rebar` stub, so the launch-failure branch is never entered
advisory.finding: The runner's reconcile-subprocess OSError branch ('Reconcile failed: could not start rebar: ...', operational_failure/rc 1, no delivery) is untested, though it is cheaply reachable with the existing stub harness (e.g. a missing/non-executable rebar on PATH). Only the delivery-nonzero and env/checkout invalid-invocation paths are covered.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make ACLI_SHA256 checksum verification mandatory (fail closed) in .gitlab-ci.yml rather than warning-and-proceeding when unset.
evidence: `.gitlab-ci.yml:33` `if [ -n "${ACLI_SHA256:-}" ]; then`
`.gitlab-ci.yml:36` `echo "ACLI_SHA256 unset; downloaded acli was not checksum-verified" >&2`

`.gitlab-ci.yml:38` `tar xzf .ci-acli/acli.tar.gz ...` then `.gitlab-ci.yml:57` pipes JIRA_API_TOKEN into `acli jira auth login` — the unverified binary is subsequently executed with the Jira credential
docs/jira-sync-setup.md:119 marks ACLI_SHA256 only '⚠️ strongly recommended | warns if unset', so the unverified path is a supported/reachable configuration
advisory.finding: New GitLab CI adapter downloads the acli binary over the network and executes it, but skips checksum verification entirely when the optional ACLI_SHA256 variable is unset (only prints a stderr warning) — a fail-open supply-chain integrity gap: an unverified remote binary is installed and run.
scenarios: Operator configures the GitLab pipeline without setting ACLI_SHA256; a MITM or compromised acli.atlassian.com serves a tampered tarball, which is extracted and executed with the JIRA_API_TOKEN piped to it

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make ACLI_SHA256 verification mandatory (fail closed) in the Jenkinsfile Bootstrap stage rather than warning-and-proceeding when unset.
evidence: `Jenkinsfile:60` `if [ -n "${ACLI_SHA256:-}" ]; then`
`Jenkinsfile:63` `echo "ACLI_SHA256 unset; downloaded acli was not checksum-verified" >&2`
`Jenkinsfile:65` `tar xzf .ci-acli/acli.tar.gz ...` then `Jenkinsfile:90` `printf '%s\n' "$JIRA_API_TOKEN" | acli jira auth login` executes the unverified binary with the credential
advisory.finding: New Jenkinsfile bridge adapter downloads and later executes the acli binary but skips checksum verification when ACLI_SHA256 is unset (only prints a stderr warning), executing an unverified remote binary — the same fail-open supply-chain integrity gap as the GitLab adapter.
scenarios: Jenkins job runs without ACLI_SHA256 configured; a tampered acli tarball is extracted and executed with the Jira credential piped in
